thread:
Ravi: ran Argyll-9b bring-up across fp16/int8/int6/int4. int4 gives ~62% token cost reduction vs fp16 but we see notable precision drop on rerank and hallucination increase on multi-hop QA. sharing quick numbers.
Alex: paste the mini scorecard when you have it. is this on the GTN slices or broader eval?
Ravi: GTN + production-like rerank slice (5k queries). rough table: 
```
variant | rel-prec@1 | rel-prec@5 | longform-f1 | halluc-rate | cost
fp16     | 0.82       | 0.76      | 0.79       | 0.012       | 1.00
int6     | 0.80       | 0.75      | 0.77       | 0.014       | 0.62
int4     | 0.73       | 0.68      | 0.70       | 0.028       | 0.38
```
Ravi: halluc-rate is fraction of outputs that include unsupported facts on our ground-truth check. int4 ~2.3x baseline on rerank slice.
Jamie: p95 latency impact? caching behavior?
Ravi: p50 similar across variants. p95 +18% on int4 for seq_len>1024. KV cache warm hit drops ~4ppt on int4.
Priya: product note  GTN cares a lot about rel-prec@1. a drop from .82 to .73 is big. can't push to GTN-critical routes.
Zoe: any mitigation experiments done? temperature/calibration, decoder constraints, or selective decoding?
Ravi: tried temperature scaling + nucleus tweak, small gains on hallucination but precision still ~6-7pts down. tried mixed-precision decode (use int4 but decode logits in fp16)  reduced halluc by ~20% of the gap but costs rise to ~0.45.
Alex: ops proposal: keep fp16/int6 for GTN-critical. enable int4 for bulk rerank and ephemeral chat with routing guard: seq_len <= 768 AND kv-hit >= 0.7 AND prompt not flagged as multi-hop. start with 3% canary on rerank endpoints.
Jamie: I'll add monitoring: rel-prec@1, rel-prec@5, hallucination-rate, p95, kv-hit, cost-per-token, and an auto-fallback signal.
Priya: define auto-fallback thresholds: if rel-prec@1 decreases by >5 absolute points OR halluc-rate > 1.8x baseline for 30m window -> immediate rollback of int4 for that route.
Alex: add a prompt classifier to avoid routing reasoning prompts to int4. simple heuristics: presence of keywords ("explain","why","step","derive"), or prompt tokens > 180. We can ship a light classifier as a Lua/regex hook in the router.
Ravi: also recommend offline slice audit: run extended eval on 50k GTN-like prompts including adversarial multi-hop set before scaling beyond 3%. decision milestone at 500k tokens served.
Zoe: operational mitigation idea: perform logits smoothing (clip topk logits) on int4 decode to reduce spurious high-prob tokens. needs infra support but can be a follow-up.
Alex: rollout plan:
- PR: infra/router#562 (routing guard + classifier) -> 3% canary on rerank (non-prod)
- run 24h smoke + 1 week monitored canary -> 500k token check
- if metrics hold -> 15% then 40% for low-sensitivity endpoints
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/router#562 -> eng-ml-canary at 2025-09-02T02:00Z :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Jamie: I'll instrument dashboards and alerts. tagging Ravi and Alex for thresholds.
Priya: product ok with this conservative approach. need to capture example failure traces for postmortem if we see recs drop.
Ravi: I'll collect failing prompts and add to the GTN holdout set. will also open a short runbook for on-call with rollback steps, link to PR and alert runbook.
Alex: agreed. owners: Alex (routing PR), Jamie (dashboards/alerts), Ravi (slices + eval), Zoe (mitigations follow-up). revisit after 500k tokens.
Ravi: thanks all. will post the slice examples and a condensed playbook in the docs channel later.
